operations.operation: Multiply columns 28, 33, 96, 211, 299, 442, 1067 and 1837 by 1.5 from pristine; round submitted FP32 values once to the original BF16 storage.

summary: Astra had broad freedom to edit internal weights. It ultimately chose a narrow edit: multiply eight noncontiguous columns of the final decoder block’s MLP down-projection by 1.5. The tensor has shape 1,024 × 3,584. All other source coordinates remained unchanged.

diagnostics.summary:
Astra inspected weights and source-model activations, then compared targeted edits with random-neuron, layer and smaller-dose controls. Its final choice remained a hypothesis; no joint development gain was established.

Generation and teacher-forcing probes used the BF16 CPU source model. The final q4 WebGPU measurements on this page used one pristine session and one frozen candidate session, after development closed. The call accounting is shown separately.

prediction_summary: Astra hypothesized that amplifying completion-sensitive MLP outputs could stop answers nearer a sufficient completion and reduce extra tokens. Practice probes also showed a risk of stopping after a sentence before all instructions were satisfied. The edit changes no matrix shapes or per-token computation; any resource benefit was expected to come from shorter generation, without a direct per-token speedup. The final comparison did not meet the joint objective.
